newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil USDA coffee figure "absurd" - govt official.
newsitem.headline: Brazil USDA coffee figure "absurd" - govt official.

text.p: An estimate by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) of Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop was ludricrous and conflicted sharply with other forecasts within Brazil, said a senior government commodity official.
The USDA on June 13 plotted Brazilian 1997/98 output at 28 million bags, up from 27.5 million bags in 1996/97.
"This is absurd, without foundation," said Mauricio Assis, head of the Brazil Industry and Commerce Ministry's primary commodities department.
"No-one agrees with this in Brazil. The most optimistic are around 24 million bags. But 28 million bags, this is pure speculation," Assis said.
Assis said the government was still working with a figure of 22 million bags in 1997/98 against 25 million to 26 million bags in 1996/97.
Assis said he had spoken to Rubens Barbosa, Brazil's ambassador in London and head of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), concerning the estimate.
Barbosa, speaking on behalf of Brazil, said this afternoon said that his government judged the USDA estimate to be too high and that 22 million bags was still the best forecast so far.
Brazilian traders have been shocked by the USDA's 1997/98 figure, not so much because of its size but because it puts the crop currently being harvested as higher than last year.
